:::{#thm-cond-linearity}

#### Linearity of conditional expectation

For jointly distributed $X$ and $Y$,
functions $h_1$ and $h_2$ whose conditional expectations given $X = x$ are defined,
and constants $a$ and $b$:

$$\E{a h_1(X, Y) + b h_2(X, Y) \mid X = x} = a\E{h_1(X, Y) \mid X = x} + b\E{h_2(X, Y) \mid X = x}$$

Evaluating both sides at $X$ gives
$\E{a h_1(X, Y) + b h_2(X, Y) \mid X} = a\E{h_1(X, Y) \mid X} + b\E{h_2(X, Y) \mid X}$.

:::

::: proof

For discrete $Y$:

$$
\ba
&\E{a h_1(X, Y) + b h_2(X, Y) \mid X = x}
\\&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} \paren{a h_1(x, y) + b h_2(x, y)} \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(definition of conditional expectation)} \\
&= a \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} h_1(x, y) \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x) + b \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} h_2(x, y) \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(distribute the sum over the terms; factor out the constants)} \\
&= a\E{h_1(X, Y) \mid X = x} + b\E{h_2(X, Y) \mid X = x}
&& \text{(definition of conditional expectation)}
\ea
$$

Splitting the sum is valid because both sums converge absolutely.
For continuous $Y$, the same steps hold with integrals over $y$ in place of the sums,
by linearity of the integral:
unlike @thm-linearity-expectation, only one variable, $y$, is integrated,
against one conditional density.

:::
